Empirical Heterogeneity Priors

Source: R/priors.R
bf_turner.Rd

Informative priors for \(\tau\) from large analyses of Cochrane reviews. They are most useful when there are few studies, where \(\tau\) is poorly identified by the data.

bf_turner() gives the log-normal priors of Turner et al. (2015) for log odds ratios (binary outcomes). bf_rhodes() gives the log-t priors of Rhodes et al. (2015) for standardised mean differences (continuous outcomes). The parameters come from bayesmeta::TurnerEtAlPrior() and bayesmeta::RhodesEtAlPrior(), so the bayesmeta package must be installed. See those functions for the outcome and comparison categories.

Usage

bf_turner(
  outcome = NA,
  comparator1 = "pharmacological",
  comparator2 = "placebo / control"
)

bf_rhodes(
  outcome = NA,
  comparator1 = "pharmacological",
  comparator2 = "placebo / control",
  area = "other"
)

Arguments

outcome

Outcome type, e.g. "all-cause mortality" for bf_turner() or "mental health outcome" for bf_rhodes(). NA gives the prior for a general outcome.

comparator1, comparator2

Intervention types compared: any of "pharmacological", "non-pharmacological" and "placebo / control".

area

Medical area for bf_rhodes(): "other", "respiratory" or "cancer".

Value

A bf_prior for \(\tau\). See bf_priors for which backends support it.

References

Turner RM, Jackson D, Wei Y, Thompson SG, Higgins JPT (2015). Predictive distributions for between-study heterogeneity and simple methods for their application in Bayesian meta-analysis. Statistics in Medicine, 34(6), 984–998.

Rhodes KM, Turner RM, Higgins JPT (2015). Predictive distributions were developed for the extent of heterogeneity in meta-analyses of continuous outcome data. Journal of Clinical Epidemiology, 68(1), 52–60.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
bf_turner("all-cause mortality", "pharmacological", "placebo / control")
bf_rhodes("mental health outcome", "non-pharmacological", "placebo / control")
} # }
